# The mask contract: every name a layer can read

*Generated by `masks/make_contract.py` from `masks/names.py` and the packs' manifests. Do not edit by hand; change `names.py` and run the generator.*

## How a layer asks for a mask

A layer is one node group. To read a mask it declares a float input called `M <Name In Title Case>` (`moss_site` becomes `M Moss Site`; `names.mask_socket(name)` makes it). That is all: the bus (`masks/bus.py`) builds one node group, `WK MASKS <material>`, per material, holding only the masks the layers on that material asked for, and wires them by name. A layer never knows which picture, frame or set a mask comes from. A mask the set has not made returns its **default** (the table below), so a layer that reads `M Water Dist` in a set without water simply sees "no water".

Every mask is a number from 0 to 1 unless the meaning says metres. Distances are scaled so 1 = "far enough that it no longer matters" (the reach is in the meaning).

## The frames

| frame | what it is | how it is looked up |
|---|---|---|
| `GP` | ground plan | A picture of the ground seen from above (4 cm per dot; 2 cm for the fine ones). Looked up by the dot's WORLD x and y. Outside the picture the default is returned. |
| `WF` | wall sheet | One picture per wall mesh (50 dots per metre across, 2 cm; the 8 cm coarse ones for broad fields), looked up by the dot's position in the OBJECT's own frame (across the front, up from the floor). Chosen by the object value `wk_frame_id`. Counts only where the surface faces the sheet's front (within about 25 degrees): `frame_valid`. Where it does not (gable ends, chimneys, roofs) the ground-plan version or the default is used. |
| `TX` | texture space | The photo material's own picture coordinates: cavity, joint line and cell number of the set's brick, stone and flag pictures (period in metres from the set file). |
| `SH` | shader | Made inside the shader from position and normal; nothing is stored. |

A name lists the frame(s) that can supply it. `GP/WF` means: on a wall the wall sheet is used where it applies, otherwise the ground plan; `WF/GP` the other way round. `OBJ` values are per object (below).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ground_height` | GP | 0.0 | Height of the top of the ground at each dot, in metres (found by dropping a ray from above onto the ground roles). Stored 16-bit over the set's z range; the bus gives metres. | from GP | from GP | from GP |
| `height` | GP/WF | 0.0 | Height of a surface point above the ground, in metres: its z minus the ground height at its x and y (wall sheets carry the baked value). | from WF | from WF | from WF |
| `slope` | GP | 0.0 | 0 = flat, 1 = a 30 degree slope (the angle of the ground's gradient over 8 cm). | 0.00 to 1.00 (mean 0.15) from GP | 0.00 to 1.00 (mean 0.18) from GP | 0.00 to 1.00 (mean 0.18) from GP |

The name `socket` of each is `names.mask_socket(name)`. `names.BY_NAME[name]` gives the row; `names.default_of(name)` the default.

## What the scale helper hands every layer (`WK SCALE`, `WK MARK WIDTH`)

Every mark is sized in **plate dots** (one dot of the plate picture the painter repaints; its size is the `plate.size` of the set file), turned into metres from the camera. The runner sets `Dot Angle` for each picture from the camera and the plate height (a 540 x 960 test picture uses the plate's value, so a mark has the same physical size in a small picture as in the plate). A layer declares any of these as inputs and the bus wires them:

| input name | meaning |
|---|---|
| `Dot Across` | metres per plate dot across the view at this point = depth x Dot Angle x Painter Widen |
| `Dot Along` | how long a dot is along the way the surface leans away = Dot Across / max(\|normal . view direction\|, 0.12) |
| `Fade Near` | 1 near the camera, 0 far (Fade Start to Fade End metres; fine detail gives way to the layer's AVERAGE tone, never to clean) |
| `Far Blend` | 0 near, 1 far (Handover Start to Handover End: 3D pieces stop and the painted far band takes over) |
| `Distance`, `Cos View` | straight distance in metres; \|normal . view direction\| |

`Painter Widen` = 0.5 / painter scale (x1.11 at 0.45, x1.25 at 0.40). `WK MARK WIDTH` (inputs Real Width, Min Dots, Dot Size, Inflate Limit; outputs Width, Fade) keeps a mark from being thinner than its minimum in dots, and fades it to the layer's average tone once the widening passes the limit.

## Per-object values (custom properties, read with an Attribute node of type Object)

The kit never edits meshes or material slots. Everything per object is a custom property, written by `apply/seed.py` (tested: EEVEE and Cycles read it equally; a missing property reads 0):

| property | meaning |
|---|---|
| `wk_seed` | 0..1 from the object's rounded world position (1 cm) and its role: renaming an object or rebuilding does not reshuffle |
| `wk_role_id` | the place of the object's role in the set's role list, from 1 (0 = no role) |
| `wk_frame_id` | which wall sheet the object reads (0 = none); written when a pack is loaded |
| `wk_zmin`, `wk_zmax` | the object's own height range in world z |
| `wk_<flag>` | per-object facts a picture cannot know, from the set file's `flags` block (for example `wk_stepped`) |
| `wk_<layer>_amount` | 1 on the roles the layer acts on, 0 on every other object (so a material shared by two kinds of object is weathered only where the set says) |
| `wk_<layer>_<dial>` | the role's multiplier for a dial the set varies by role (1 where the role has none) |

## The layer's own sockets (see `apply/layer_template.py`)

In: the bundle `Colour`, `Roughness`, `Specular IOR Level`, `Coat Weight`, `Normal`, `Metallic`, `Wet Normal`; the masks by name; `Wet Mask`, `Puddle Mask` (a layer placed after the water layer gets them; slot A reads 0); the scale inputs; the dials, one input each in Title Case (`Amount`, `Seed`, `Inflate Limit`, `Fade Start`, `Fade End`, `Wet Follow`, then the layer's own). Out: the same bundle (an output left unconnected passes its input through) and `Mask` (the layer's own mask, raw, for debug views and the measures).

Dials: 12 layers, 152 rows in `apply/dial_table.json` (generated from the plan's one list; the look files carry the values).

## Shared rules

* **Exact zero.** `moss_site`, `weed_site` and `lichen_site` are exactly 0.0 wherever `footfall` is 0.6 or more, `crown` 0.7 or more or `keepclear` 0.5 or more (`algae_site` where `keepclear` is 0.5 or more). A habitat field is a product with a gate, never a threshold on noise, so the zero is exact; the reader tests it when it builds the pack.
* **Amount 0 changes nothing.** Every mix factor in a layer is a product containing the amount; nothing can become NaN.
* **No Bevel, Ambient Occlusion or Pointiness nodes.** Edges come from `edge_dist`, `piece_gap` and `step_edge` (made from the real geometry, once).
* **Frames.** A mask is only as sharp as its frame: GP 4 cm (fine 2 cm), WF 2 cm (coarse 8 cm), TX the photo's own pixels.
